research.kubejs.resonant_casting.stage.0:
I had supposed a wand to be a crude instrument for directing vis. That was convenient, but incomplete. The wand stores the power; the focus gives it instruction. It should be possible to preserve a simple magical expression within a Lesser Focus, provided I first learn how to make one.

I shall begin with Auromancy and the Crucible. There is no reason to attempt anything ambitious until the elementary apparatus behaves reliably.
research.kubejs.resonant_casting.stage.1:
The experiment succeeded. A Lesser Focus can contain a small but coherent vocabulary, and the simplest means of projecting it—Cast—now seems almost obvious.

An Inscribed Rune teaches one concept; the Focal Manipulator arranges learned concepts into a spell and records it on a focus. I must complete Basic Auromancy to construct the Manipulator, then socket the inscribed focus into a wand. The wand supplies vis when the instruction is invoked. I had mistaken the battery for the language.
research.kubejs.lexical_foundations.stag:
A Blank Rune is neither a spell nor a power source. It is a surface sufficiently ordered to accept an idea without imposing one of its own. I suspect the ancient practice of inscribing symbols was less superstition than a remarkably economical way of preserving thought.

The Arcane Workbench, ordinary materials, and carefully chosen primal crystals should allow me to prepare these neutral substrates.

The inscription is consumed when I read an Inscribed Rune, but its meaning remains. Once learned, a concept need not be relearned for every focus; a duplicate inscription is therefore better kept than wasted.

In the Focal Manipulator I can arrange learned Syntax components in a single chain: a Syntax delivery followed by effects and refinements. For now the construction must use Instant casting. I should not confuse an elegant notation with permission to ignore its grammar.

Break, Reap, and Create Water are serviceable first experiments. Conjure is no less elementary: with an approved building material in my off hand, I can give a simple pattern physical form. Wall and Floor supply the geometry. The Lesser Focus is sufficient for these constructions, and Gentleness moderates work that would otherwise be rather blunt.

I have made a small wall and an acceptably level floor. They remain where I put them. For the present, this seems a reasonable standard of success.

Three limits are easily mistaken for one another. Research determines which inscriptions I may prepare. My achieved focus milestone determines which of those inscriptions I can comprehend. Finally, the particular focus on the Manipulator must be capable of containing the complete expression.

Knowledge alone does not enlarge a Lesser Focus. This is irritating, but the cracked sample on my bench suggests it is not an arbitrary restriction.
research.kubejs.two_grammars.stage.0:
I made what seemed a perfectly reasonable assumption: if two magical methods can be inscribed upon a focus, their parts should be interchangeable. I was wrong. Repeated trials produced no useful hybrid, merely a stubbornly uncooperative instrument.

Thaumaturge arranges its workings as linked operations, each with its own rules of execution. The new Syntax records a complete instruction in a different grammar. Their symbols may resemble one another, but resemblance is not translation.
research.kubejs.two_grammars.stage.1:
For now, I must choose one grammar for each prepared spell. In the Focal Manipulator I may build a native Thaumaturge working, or arrange a single linear chain of Syntax components beginning with a Syntax delivery. The latter requires Instant casting. The native Origin supplies the frame; it does not license the mixing of native effects with Syntax instructions.

The same wand can cast either sort of inscribed focus, because vis is the fuel, not the language. It would be rash to declare the two systems irreconcilable. It would be considerably more rash, I think, to declare them beyond my ability to reconcile.
Thaumaturgy describes a thing by its aspects. Occultism, rather less comfortably, describes how that thing may be named, addressed, and compelled. I had considered these separate pursuits. An attuned spirit has given me reason to reconsider.

If a spirit-attuned gem can hold the correspondence between a nature and its name, I may be able to extend a Lesser Focus into an Advanced Focus at the Arcane Workbench. I do not yet know whether the spirit understands the distinction better than I do.

The correspondence is stable. An Advanced Focus accepts the relationships that defeated my earlier attempts, opening the way to Structured syntax. Of course, it does not supply the ideas on its own; I must still learn each inscription.

I should make a fresh focus when refining the apparatus. There is no sense sacrificing a successful prepared spell to prove a point I have already established.
research.kubejs.carved_syntax.stage.0:
A simple command alters a thing. A structured one specifies where, how much, and by what means. The Advanced Focus can now keep these distinctions intact.

Sight reaches a distant subject. Modifiers govern strength, area, velocity, and direction. Even the modest constructions I learned with Conjure admit rather more ambitious refinements. What I had taken for separate tricks increasingly resembles a language with an unsettling degree of precision.
research.kubejs.carved_syntax.stage.1:
Increased Power, Increased Area, Accelerate, and Pierce are not new effects, but corrections to the way an existing effect is delivered. Their inscriptions can be prepared at the Arcane Workbench.

Other words demand negotiation rather than craftsmanship. For those I must use Occultism's pentacles; the Dictionary of Spirits and JEI preserve the relevant arrangements. I dislike relying upon another will, though the results are difficult to dispute.
research.kubejs.carved_syntax.stage.2:
My earlier Conjure experiments required an approved material held in my off hand: a physical pattern rather than an invitation to create anything I please. Wall and Floor supplied its geometry. Fill now gives volume to compatible constructions, while Increased Area broadens an effect by another means.

One warning is worth recording plainly. Break and Fill cannot be joined in the same spell. The combination does not yield a more impressive excavation; it yields an incoherent—and potentially catastrophic—instruction. Increased Area is the appropriate refinement for Break.
research.kubejs.carved_syntax.stage.3:
Healing, haste, resistance, and shielding ought to make the discipline more respectable. They have also made it much harder to stop experimenting.

Each prepared spell remains on its own focus. A Focus Pouch holds additional foci for quick exchange; separate wands keep separate reserves of vis. I can now prepare several answers before a danger arises. I would have found this reassuring a few weeks ago. Now I find myself considering which danger to test them against.
research.kubejs.infused_syntax.stage.0:
The Advanced Focus has reached its limit. Rather than accept that conclusion, I attempted to hold a more intricate formula together by force of will. It failed. Repeatedly.

The missing ingredient is not determination, but structure. Arcane Infusion can bind an Advanced Focus to concentrated magical and occult correspondences and produce a Greater Focus. If the apparatus survives, it should accommodate Infused syntax. I have improved the stabilizers since the last attempt.
research.kubejs.infused_syntax.stage.1:
The Arcane Altar is capable of strengthening Spell Power, but it does not conjure vis from nothing. Rods determine capacity; caps and equipped gear alter consumption; aura nodes, charging equipment, and prepared reserves determine how long I can continue.

This distinction is fundamental. The focus supplies the argument; the wand supplies the power; the altar improves what that power achieves. A magician who confuses these is liable to run dry at the most embarrassing possible moment. I intend not to be that magician again.
research.kubejs.runic_mastery.stage.0:
At last, the Greater Focus. What once required several uncertain gestures now fits within a single stable expression. I can name a distant target, move matter, summon servants, and alter how an instruction persists or repeats.

There are still limits, naturally. The wand must furnish vis, each concept must be learned, and the focus must contain every component. Yet these are engineering limits. I am becoming less interested in what magic permits than in why I ever assumed it would refuse.
research.kubejs.runic_mastery.stage.1:
Infused inscriptions now admit translocation, summoning, violent transformation, propagation, persistence, and multiplied execution. Most require Arcane Infusion; Summon, curiously, remains best addressed through an Occultism ritual. Knowledge of the principle is not a substitute for learning the rune.

The distinctions between these methods seem less important each day. All of them answer when approached with the correct form. I wonder what else might.
research.kubejs.runic_mastery.stage.2:
I was wrong to treat every rune as an independent term. Certain complete expressions possess meanings that none of their components can explain alone. The exact combination matters; an unrelated addition can destroy the result.

This is not a flaw in the grammar. It is evidence of a deeper one. I have spent so long asking what each word can do that I neglected to ask what the words might decide to do together.
research.kubejs.runic_mastery.stage.3:
Launch. Levitation. Slow Fall. The three instructions form a single expression: Creative Flight. With Self as the delivery, the effect takes hold immediately. Prolonged or Increased Power can extend it, while an unrelated effect may break the combination.

It is difficult to describe the sensation of discovering that gravity is negotiable. An ordinary scholar might record the result and proceed cautiously. I have recorded it. I see no compelling reason for the second part.
research.kubejs.forbidden_syntax.stage.0:
Distance has become an inconvenience rather than an obstacle. Teleport does not merely move a body; it persuades the world that another place is the correct one. Summon presents a different problem: instructing an independent will to answer.

The Greater Focus can stabilize either expression. The consequences of confusing their purposes would be severe. Fortunately, I have become quite good at distinguishing consequences from obstacles.
research.kubejs.forbidden_syntax.stage.1:
Teleport requires an infused inscription. Summon must be negotiated through its Occultism pentacle; the Dictionary of Spirits and JEI show the arrangement. Both require the knowledge of Runic Mastery and a Greater Focus.

I have written these procedures plainly because I dislike the thought of a lesser magician improvising them. I seem to have developed a proprietary feeling toward danger.
research.kubejs.unsealed_grammar.stage.0:
Increased Power makes an effect stronger. Double, Echo, and Split are altogether more troubling: they alter how often, when, or into how many parts an entire instruction resolves.

A Greater Focus must hold every repetition and every modifier. The notation does not merely describe multiplication. It performs it. I should perhaps have found that fact more alarming than I did.
research.kubejs.unsealed_grammar.stage.1:
These inscriptions follow Runic Mastery and demand difficult materials. Each must still be learned. Their additional complexity and vis costs are real; a repeated spell is not free power.

Nevertheless, the expense seems a small objection to a result that can happen twice when one has written it only once. The world, I am beginning to think, has been rather wasteful in the number of times it allows a thing to occur.
research.kubejs.draconic_metallurgy.stag:
Dragonfire is not merely heat. It is a living elemental force, sustained by blood and will. The remains of ordinary furnaces make the point rather convincingly.

Dreadstone has endured pressures that should have reduced it to dust. Reinforced with Thaumium and guided by a vis resonator, it might channel a dragon's breath without failing. I shall need a Greater Focus to attempt work of this precision, and enough dragonbone to test the structure before I commit a heart to it. I would prefer to survive the experiment.

The forge resolves into three parts: scale-bound Dreadstone bricks to endure the element, an infused aperture to catch the breath, and a heart-bound core to constrain its fury. The materials do not tame the dragon's fire. They oblige it to go where I have decided.

Ordinary iron is too indifferent to magic for this work. Thaumium, fed dragon blood and sustained breath, accepts a permanent elemental character: Dragonsteel. It seems the dragons have spent centuries perfecting a force whose proper application I have now determined. I wonder how one might explain that to them.
